items.title: Show HN: Musset, open-source Scrivener alternative with an AI that never writes (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: I'm writing my first novel and could not find an app that fit my workflow: quiet like iA Writer, organized like Scrivener, and with AI so I can discuss my book while I write it. It allows me to feel less "alone" and have a sounding board while I write. - A book is a folder of plain Markdown files. Musset commits to a git repo, tracks versions and drafts without you having to know git. - Revisions are CriticMarkup inside the text. It manages docx revisions too, so your editor can edit a Word doc and you import their comments. - PDFs are typeset using Typst, embedded in the app, following each language's typographic rules. - Spelling and grammar are checked using LanguageTool, also embedded. - Mac/Word, WordStar, vi and Emacs keyboard modes. The AI is optional and uses your Codex or Claude Code CLI. It comments, leaves margin notes, and checks continuity and your chapters against your style rules. It's GPL-3.0 and free during the beta. When or if it reaches 1.0, if there is sufficient interest, the idea is to make it a small one-time payment ($9.90). There is a paid sync service (git hosting) that lets you share a book with beta readers and editors. Download: https://musset.app I'd love to have some feedback! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50586323 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

items.title: Tell HN: OpenRouter prompts to Minimax may have been read (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: I received the following email from OpenRouter and it appears authentic. There is no public page or blog post. -- Title: Requests you sent to MiniMax models may have been read Hi there, A security researcher placed unique test URLs in prompts sent to MiniMax models from July to October 2026. A third party accessed those URLs 40 to 130 hours after the requests were sent, whether MiniMax served a request directly or another provider forwarded it to MiniMax. With one exception, the same tests on other models at those providers were not accessed, and none of the AWS test keys were used. Your account sent [redacted] requests to MiniMax models through MiniMax and Novita, from [redacted] to [redacted] UTC. AtlasCloud, Novita and StreamLake have told us they forwarded OpenRouter requests for MiniMax models to MiniMax. Based on what the researcher and these providers have reported, the issue sits with MiniMax and the providers that forwarded to it, not with OpenRouter. We are passing on what they have told us. MiniMax told StreamLake that content moderation was enabled on its endpoints before October 22 and that it has since enabled Zero Data Retention. We have asked MiniMax for its own account and have not received one. This means a third party may have read the prompts and outputs of these requests. While we investigate, we have removed the Zero Data Retention label from these MiniMax-model endpoints. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50585962 Points: 7 # Comments: 2

items.title: Ask HN: I have been unemployed for 2y. 15 years of experience, US. What to do? (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: I'm Senior software engineer in the US (DMV area), with 15y of experience. Worked for Fortune 50+ company and bunch of mid-size companies. Been unemployed for 2y and can't find a job, within those 2 years, I pretty much spent my savings that I've saved through years, maybe have 4-5 months left to support my household. Currently, I tutor math and probably about to start working as manager in pizzaria. In Jan 2025, I quit from a mid-size insurance tech company(1000+) after working there for almost 4y, because I was tipped off the they were about to start layoffs and they did. Well, since then I have zero luck finding any job in SWE. At this point, I have massive gap in my resume that I can't explain to recruiters, I can still code (C#/.NET/AWS) and learned the AI, but who cares if date of my last employment is Jan2025. What should I do ? If you have an alternative path (something completely different from SWE or SWE adjacent) that pays "well", I would like to hear. items.title: Show HN: OpenComputer - an open source alternative to Devin (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: Hi HN! Utpal here, I'm one of the founders of OpenComputer. OpenComputer is an open source cloud coding agent for teams that can run in your own cloud account (AWS, GCP, Azure). We run the agent harness and the sandbox on the same durable VM (architecture in the docs [1]). First commit lands in 24s; the alternatives we benchmarked took 53-72s (benchmarks below [2]). Two other choices: - One VM per team, scalable horizontally. Sessions are isolated in git worktrees. - Session files are backed up to a repo after every turn, so any session can resume on another VM. We noticed that past ~640 session-hours a month, one always-on 4 vCPU VM is cheaper than per-session E2B sandboxes, for example. So at scale, this setup would not only be faster than current SOTA coding agents, but also more cost-efficient. Feel free to try via cloud for free [4] or self host. We would love any and all feedback, and happy to answer any questions! Full demo below [3]. [1]: https://docs.opencomputer.dev/getting-started/architecture [2]: https://opencomputer.dev/blog/cloud-agents-as-fast-as-local/ [3]: https://x.com/IgorZIJ/status/2121309785882591711 [4]: https://app.opencomputer.dev Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50581403 Points: 90 # Comments: 24
